title: Key-value store over a crash-safe append-only log
prompt:
Finish the store in `src/`, which keeps its durable state as an in-memory append-only log of framed records. `src/index.js` re-exports `HEADER_BYTES`, `StoreError`, `crc32`, `isRecord`, `encodeRecord` and `decodeLog` from `src/log.js` and `KvStore` from `src/store.js`; keep that surface. `StoreError` extends `Error`, sets `name` to `'StoreError'`, carries a `code` and is constructed as `(code, message)`. A record is `{ t: 'put', k, v }` or `{ t: 'del', k }`, where `k` is a non-empty string and a put always carries a `v` property; `isRecord` reports exactly that. `crc32(bytes)` is the standard reflected CRC-32 with polynomial 0xEDB88320, initial value 0xFFFFFFFF and a final complement, returned unsigned, so the checksum of the ASCII bytes of `123456789` is 0xCBF43926 and the checksum of no bytes is 0. `encodeRecord(record)` frames a record as an 8-byte header followed by the UTF-8 JSON of the record: a big-endian uint32 payload byte length, then the big-endian uint32 CRC-32 of that payload. Both `crc32` and `decodeLog` throw `'BAD_INPUT'` with message `bytes must be a Uint8Array` for anything else, and `encodeRecord` throws `'BAD_RECORD'` with message `record must be a put or del entry`.

`decodeLog(bytes)` reads records from the front of a log and returns `{ records, bytesUsed, truncated }`. It must never throw for a `Uint8Array`, no matter what the bytes contain, because a log may be cut off at any byte or damaged in place. Scanning stops at the first frame that is not fully intact: fewer than 8 bytes left for a header, fewer bytes left than the header's length field claims, a payload whose CRC does not match, a payload that is not valid JSON, or a payload that decodes to something `isRecord` rejects. `bytesUsed` is the number of bytes belonging to the records that were returned, and `truncated` says whether the scan stopped early. Consequently the records decoded from any prefix of a log are always a prefix of the records decoded from the whole log.

`KvStore` keeps live keys in memory and mirrors every accepted mutation into the log. `put(key, value)` appends a put record and returns the store so calls chain; `delete(key)` returns whether the key existed and appends a del record only when it did. Keys must be non-empty strings (`'BAD_KEY'`, `key must be a non-empty string`) and are validated by `put`, `get`, `has` and `delete` alike. A value must be representable as JSON without loss (`'BAD_VALUE'`, `value is not serializable`): a string, a boolean, `null`, a finite number, or an array or plain object built recursively from those; anything else, including `undefined`, `NaN`, infinities, functions, dates, maps, class instances and cyclic structures, is rejected. Stored values never alias caller values, so mutating a value after storing it, or mutating a value handed back by `get`, `entries` or `snapshot`, cannot change the store. `keys()` returns live keys in ascending order, `entries()` the matching key-value pairs, `size` their count, and the `log` getter a fresh copy of the log bytes. `stats()` returns `{ records, liveKeys, deadRecords }`, where `records` counts the records in the current log and `deadRecords` is `records - liveKeys`.

`KvStore.replay(bytes)` rebuilds a store from the intact prefix of a log: it applies the decoded records in order and keeps exactly those bytes as its log, so replaying a store's own log reproduces its entries, its stats and its bytes, and replaying a log cut at any byte yields the state of some earlier moment rather than an error. `compact()` rewrites the log as one put per live key in ascending key order, leaves the visible state untouched, and returns `{ before, after, reclaimed }` in bytes; after it, `stats()` reports no dead records and compacting again reclaims nothing. `snapshot()` returns `{ version: 1, entries }` with the entries in ascending key order, and the static `fromSnapshot(snapshot)` rebuilds a store whose log is already compact. Snapshot loading validates as it goes: a non-object snapshot throws `'BAD_SNAPSHOT'` with message `snapshot must be an object`, a version other than 1 gives `unsupported snapshot version`, a non-array `entries` gives `snapshot entries must be an array`, an entry that is not a two-element array gives `each snapshot entry must be a key and a value`, keys and values are checked as `put` checks them, and a repeated key gives `duplicate key in snapshot: <key>`.
